title: Crispy Salmon & Sweet Corn Cakes with Roasted Broccoli & Lemon Couscous
summary: Golden pan-seared salmon-and-corn patties made with boneless canned salmon, served with oven-roasted broccoli and quick lemon couscous. Dairy-free, 35–40 minutes total and about 25–30 minutes active.
ingredients: 4 cans (5 oz each) kosher-certified boneless, skinless salmon, drained
3/4 cup sweet corn kernels, thawed if frozen
1/2 cup kosher-certified pareve panko breadcrumbs, plus 1–2 tbsp if needed
1 1/4 cups water or kosher-certified pareve vegetable broth (or follow package directions)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss broccoli florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 18–22 minutes, turning once.

While broccoli roasts, drain salmon well. In a bowl, gently mix salmon, corn, eggs, panko, pareve mayonnaise, Dijon, scallions if using, half the lemon zest, garlic powder and a pinch of pepper. Shape into 10–12 small patties. If loose, add 1–2 tbsp more panko and press firmly.

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook patties in two batches, about 3–4 minutes per side, until browned, firm and hot through; aim for 160°F in the center because they contain egg. Avoid flipping before a crust forms.

Meanwhile bring 1 1/4 cups water or pareve broth to a boil. Stir in couscous, cover, remove from heat and rest 5 minutes (or follow package instructions). Fluff and add remaining lemon zest, 1–2 tbsp lemon juice, parsley if using and salt to taste.
Serve 2–3 salmon cakes per adult with broccoli and couscous. Offer lemon wedges or a little pareve mayonnaise for dipping.
child_friendly_modifications: Make a few nugget-sized cakes with finely chopped corn and no scallions; offer ketchup or pareve mayonnaise for dipping. Serve couscous plain and broccoli in small, tender florets. For the 3-year-old, break cakes into bite-size pieces and check for any remaining bones even with boneless canned salmon. Avoid whole hard corn kernels if the child has difficulty chewing them.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly within 2 hours. Eat refrigerated cakes within 3–4 days, reheating in a 375°F oven or air fryer until hot throughout. Flake leftover cakes into a pareve pita with cucumber and lemon dressing for lunch; store couscous and broccoli separately for best texture.
